item.content:encoded:
I realize that I hadn't upvoted this story before and now, that makes me wonder if I'd already upvoted the other parts of Incident Zero and some of the Resurrection stories that I'd already read.

Honestly, I will not say all the reasons of my upvote because they fall under the same "genuine and intense love for this canon" category. But I will just say that the end sequence is just really powerful for me.

I'm one of those who believe that the unknown man at this sequence is "IRL Clef" and seeing him, thinking about his journey, the rough paths, the multiple roads and, finally, the fact that yes, all of this was worth it (all the words in this sequence could be, if we take this way, a metaphor of what Clef had done for the site since 2008) made it, like I say, extremely powerful. Because we see a man who seems reconcilied with his past, with the mistakes, with the "Mary-Sue" eras, with all.

And this is why this ending is just perfect. Naturally, maybe you won't agree with me, there is no canon, after all. But this is why I love it and why the upvote is deserved with extreme, extreme gusto.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
didn't actually happen

All I can say is that this makes me regret I'm not presently finishing the rest of my own Resurrection tales at a very good pace, because then I'd have some thematic answers for that statement.

That said, that's not correct — Able does in fact slaughter all of Omega-7 in Resurrection's canon history. (He does so after the events of this story — "after" in context of Able's personal timeline, mind.) That event shapes the characters of several people involved in the story, Iris in particular.

I could say more, but I still want to write or co-write the stories that follow up on this (hope springs eternal) and elaboration may or may not spoil future stories.
